caption:
Your gamble, readable 0.5 s early.
Nature Neuroscience, 15 Sept 2026. Starkweather, Chang, Knight; UCSF and UC Berkeley.

Six patients implanted for surgical monitoring played a video game with bombs and treasure chests. Two patches of orbitofrontal cortex about 2 cm apart did opposite jobs and together predicted the choice about 0.5 s before it was made. No free-will claim. Would you want to see your own signal?

#neuroscience #brain #decisions #science
voiceover_script: A brain signal can predict your gamble about half a second before the choice is made. Six patients, already fitted with electrodes for surgical monitoring, played a video game with hallways, bombs and treasure chests. Take the risk, or avoid it. In the orbitofrontal cortex, two patches about two centimetres apart did opposite jobs. One became active before a risky choice, the other before a safe one. Together, they predicted the decision roughly half a second before it was made. Six patients, one video game, and no claim about free will. Starkweather, Chang and Knight, at UCSF and UC Berkeley.
